descriptor: Air-conditioning and refrigeration for Navy warships and submarines (BSE SME)
lede: A Karad company that indigenised air-conditioning for Scorpene submarines and now holds about 64% of naval HVAC orders, riding India's warship build-out. FY26 met every guidance number, but cash stays tied up for a year in working capital, the founding family is paid generously, and the stock trades at 64x earnings.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue +55% to ₹154 Cr, EBITDA margin 21-22% and PAT ₹22 Cr, all within or above guidance; H2 alone ₹103 Cr at a 26% margin. Order book ₹271 Cr (1.8x revenue), a ~₹1,000 Cr bid pipeline, and approvals from all three naval directorates that few rivals hold.

Working capital ~370 days and operating cash flow negative in three of four years; EBITDA margin has fallen from 31% (FY24) as high-margin spares shrank to 7% of sales. Key managers' pay was ₹4.6 Cr (about a fifth of profit), and shareholders are asked to lift the managerial pay cap to 15% of profit.
~64x trailing earnings and ~43x EV/EBITDA, against Marine Electricals at 103x, Blue Star at 62x and ICE Make at 96x.

blocks.text: Shree Refrigerations designs, makes, installs and services AC plants, refrigeration plants, ship-wide HVAC and control panels for Indian Navy warships and submarines, both new builds and retrofits, plus test rooms and calorimeters for refrigeration makers. It is entering data-centre cooling as Smardt's partner for oil-free chillers and is Danfoss Turbocor's authorised service partner.

items.text: Spares and service earn the highest margins; they fell from ~30-40% of revenue to 7% in FY26 and are targeted back at 15-20%.
Most contracts are fixed-price over 2-3 years, so metal inflation hurts.
Deliveries follow shipyard schedules, so H2 has been ~70% of the year.
Moved from test equipment into naval HVAC in 2012-17; supplied P-17A frigates and Scorpene submarines.
IPO on BSE SME in 2025 (₹95 Cr fresh issue); revenue from ₹45 Cr (FY22) to ₹154 Cr (FY26).
New 50,000 sq ft plant at Karad (₹25 Cr) from June 2026, expandable to 1 lakh sq ft.

items.text: Navy orders slip: ~₹190 Cr at a 9% margin (₹17 Cr), valued at 25x.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

A real niche leader with credible delivery against guidance and a long naval runway. The valuation already prices ~40% growth, while cash conversion, falling margins and generous family pay argue for caution; a data-centre win or a return of spares revenue would change the picture.
